_comment: Per-app vocabulary the recorder uses to make a FIRST GUESS at which
recorded clicks are irreversible. It lives here, beside policy.json,
rather than in recorder.py because it is target-specific knowledge, not
recording logic -- a second app gets a second entry, not a code change.
This is a heuristic and it is not a determination. Verb matching cannot
reliably detect irreversibility in a legacy UI: the same word commits on
one screen and navigates on another, and an app is free to label its
post button 'OK'. The recorder proposes; a human disposes during the
draft -> approved review. That is what capability.status: 'draft' is for,
and why every decision below is written into the artifact where a
reviewer will see it rather than only into a log.
post_like_verbs  matched with word boundaries, case-insensitively,
against the resolved accessible name of a clicked
control. A match records the step as risk: 'risky'.
near_miss_verbs  considered and NOT treated as risky. Recorded as
near-misses so a reviewer can see what the heuristic
weighed, not just what it concluded. 'Submit' sits here
on purpose: it is the generic verb for sending any form,
including a search, so treating it as a commit would
mark read-only lookups risky and block them under
require_confirmation. An app where Submit really does
mean post moves it into post_like_verbs for that app.

_note: Inherits the default set. CoreServ's search form submits with a button
named 'Submit', which is exactly the read-only case the default set is
